title: Three in Four FDA Authorizations of AI Medical Devices Were in Radiology, Study Led by GigHz Founder Finds
key_facts: GigHz, a physician-founded software and research company, announced findings of a study led by its founder Pouyan Golshani, MD, published in Cureus on 13 Jul 2026.
76.5% of 1,430 FDA AI/ML-enabled device authorization records (Sep 1995 to Dec 2025) were reviewed by the Radiology panel (1,094 records).
Radiology, Cardiovascular and Neurology panels together accounted for 90.6%.
The authors counted 331 authorizations in 2025; annual authorizations averaged 1.8 a year in 1995-2014 and 264 a year in 2023-2025.
Of 740 companies, 502 (67.8%) had a single authorized device.
No authorizations were recorded under a psychiatry or behavioral health panel.
The study counts authorizations, not adoption or patient benefit, and the FDA list is not comprehensive.
quote_evidence: The analysis measures authorization records, not clinical adoption, patient benefit or physician replacement.
The study describes authorization patterns; it does not test what caused them.
why_it_matters_hint: Almost all FDA-cleared medical AI is in radiology, according to a study from a company that builds clinical AI software.
event_date: Study published 13 Jul 2026; press release 6 Oct 2026
notes: Company press release about an older paper; author has commercial interest in clinical AI (disclosed in the release). Score lowered by 1 for age.
